text:
maria: heads up — since we flipped the central egress NGW for prod clusters, some jobs are failing when they talk to Interface VPC Endpoints (S3/ECR). getting TLS handshake resets and a bunch of client side timeouts.

sam: seen that in staging too. logs show many retries to vpce IPs then connection reset. did we accidentally route VPCE IPs to the NGW? :thinking_face:

alex: quick check — run on a broken node: `ip route get 3.5.140.22` (vpce IP). on one node it returns via 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gw (x.x.x.x). that means SNAT is happening.

priya: oh — if SNAT is changing the source to the NGW EIP, the endpoint SGs that only allow cluster CIDR will drop the traffic. can you `curl -v` the vpce IP from a pod and paste tcpdump from the endpoint ENI?

maria: pasted snippets: `curl: (56) Received reset` and from `tcpdump -n -i eth0 src x.x.x.x and dst 3.5.140.22`: shows source=100.96.2.14 (pod) -> 3.5.140.22 on node, then on the VPC ENI side the packets show src=54.239.123.7 (NAT EIP) -> dst 3.5.140.22. so the response path is using the NAT.

oncall: infra-bot noticed a deploy 1945678800 that changed iptables MASQUERADE rules on nodes to force SNAT for all outbound to central egress (intended). maybe that rule is too broad and matches VPCE IPs.

sam: can you `iptables -t nat -S`? my hunch: kube-proxy or our egress setup added `-A POSTROUTING -s 100.96.0.0/11 -j MASQUERADE` without excluding the VPCE CIDRs.

alex: confirmed: `-A POSTROUTING -s 100.96.0.0/11 -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE` and there's no exception for 3.5.140.0/24 (vpce range). so traffic to the interface endpoint is being SNATed to the NGW EIP and endpoint SGs are rejecting.

priya: two short fixes: 1) add a narrow exception in iptables NAT POSTROUTING to NOT MASQUERADE traffic with dst in the VPCE ranges, or 2) update the VPCE SGs to allow the NGW EIP range (less ideal for long term).

maria: we tried option 2 (quick patch) — added inbound rule to vpce SG to allow the handful of NGW EIPs. that immediately reduced failures but still saw Some connection resets from long-lived sockets.

oncall: why long-lived sockets break: because existing connections had been SNATed then SG hit changed semantics — existing conntrack entries still referenced old tuples and the endpoint sometimes responded to previously SNATed ports that didn't match. need conntrack flush as well.

sam: sequence to mitigate now: 1) add SG rule to allow NGW EIPs 2) push iptables change: insert rule before MASQUERADE `-m iprange --dst-range 3.5.140.0-3.5.140.255 -j RETURN` (exclude vpce) 3) flush conntrack for related tuples on nodes `conntrack -D -d 3.5.140.22` 4) restart affected pods.

alex: I'm pushing an iptables change via the egress DaemonSet with the exclusion. command: `iptables -t nat -I POSTROUTING 1 -m iprange --dst-range 3.5.140.0-3.5.140.255 -j RETURN && iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 100.96.0.0/11 -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE` — tested on a node, `curl` to vpce now succeeds and the packet traces show source still the pod IP (no SNAT).

priya: rolling that to all nodes now. I'll also open a follow-up with networking to get the canonical list of VPCE CIDRs per region so we can template the exclusion (don't want fragile hard-coded IPs).

maria: thanks — after the roll and conntrack clears, backfills completed. job failure rate down to normal. :tada:

oncall: action items recorded: `- restrict MASQUERADE to exclude VPCE CIDRs (eng-infra)`, `- query AWS for vpce ip ranges per region and bake into egress config (eng-infra/infra)`, `- evaluate whether endpoint SGs should include central NAT EIPs (short-term)`, `- add automated conntrack flush step to egress rollout (sre)`.

infra-bot: deployed egress-iptables-update daemonset v2.1 to prod cluster prod-us-east-1 (rollout started).

maria: follow up — let's schedule a postmortem doc with the root cause and config diffs. noted that our default assumption "all outbound gets SNAT" must explicitly exclude intra-vpc interface endpoints.

sam: small note for the doc: include `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc> --query 'VpcEndpoints[*].DnsEntries'` and `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values="*vpce*"` as quick ops checks.

priya: will do. closing the thread once rollout finishes and metrics look green. :white_check_mark:
